features.name: Habit list and date matrix
steps: An empty state is shown when there are no habits at first
The habit appears in the list after being created
Each row corresponds to a Habit and each column to a day
Scrolling the date into the past shows the historical states
After adding the day's record the corresponding cell and habit statistics change immediately
features.expected: The empty state and the with-data state must be distinguishable; the date columns correspond one-to-one with the real dates and the history can be traced back; after checking in the corresponding cell and statistics update immediately; all records persist and stay consistent after a restart.

features.name: Create a "done or not" habit
steps: Tap +
Choose "done or not"
Set the title, question, color, frequency, reminders, and notes
Save
The new Habit appears on the home page
Re-entering the edit page restores all the settings
features.expected: After saving, the new Habit must appear in the list; fields such as title, question, color, frequency, reminder, and notes persist and are restored when re-entering the edit page; missing required fields should block saving or give feedback.

features.name: Create a quantifiable habit
steps: Quantifiable
Set the title, question, unit, target value, goal type, frequency, reminders, and color
Save
The main list switches to showing numeric progress instead of an ordinary Yes/No state
The goal statistics appear on the details page
features.expected: The quantifiable Habit's main list must show numeric progress rather than Yes/No; settings such as the target value and unit persist; the detail statistics must be derived from the actual records and the goal, and after changing the goal all related statistics are recomputed.

features.name: Flexible frequencies and schedule rules
steps: Create habits such as daily, every other day, or N times per week
Decide which dates need action based on the historical completion
After a non-daily habit reaches the required frequency, the remaining days can show a "not required" state
After changing the frequency the future date rules are recomputed. The official Loop explicitly supports flexible schedules such as daily, every other day, and several times per week. GitHub
features.expected: The frequency rules must genuinely affect which dates need completion; after an N-times-per-week habit meets its quota the remaining days show as "not required" without penalty; after changing the frequency the future schedule is recomputed without damaging the historical records.

features.name: Binary habit check-in state machine
steps: Tap to record today's Yes/No Habit
Incomplete becomes completed
Toggling again undoes/changes that day's state
The history, score, home grid, and detail statistics update at the same time
The records are preserved after a restart
features.expected: Checking in is a state toggle rather than accumulation, and tapping repeatedly undoes it; the home grid, detail statistics, and score must stay consistent using the same record; the record persists after a restart.

features.name: Numeric recording for a quantifiable habit
steps: Enter the day's value for a "running"-type Habit
Save value + unit
Compare with the goal
The daily and periodic statistics update
After modifying the day's value all related statistics are recomputed rather than a separate independent record being created
features.expected: Modifying the value on the same day must update the original record rather than creating a second one; the value and unit are saved as a pair; the met determination comes from comparing the value with the goal; all statistics are recomputed immediately on modification.

features.name: Quantifiable goal direction
steps: Set the goal to a type such as "at least"
When the entered value reaches the goal it shows met, and below the goal it shows not met
Different goal directions use the corresponding comparison logic
The goals and scores in the details are derived from the actual values
features.expected: For "at least" goals the met state is shown when the value reaches or exceeds the target, and the opposite for "at most" goals; the met state must be derived from the actual records and the goal; after changing the goal value or type the historical met states are recomputed.

features.name: Skip Day
steps: Enable "skip days"
A day switches from incomplete to Skip
That day shows an independent skipped state
Skip is not treated as success or failure and preserves the corresponding semantics of the Habit Score / streak
Toggling again restores the normal recording. The official FAQ clearly states that Skip Day does not change the Score and does not break the streak. GitHub
features.expected: Skip must be an independent state from completion and failure; per the official semantics Skip does not change the Score and does not break the streak; the statistics update immediately after toggling Skip; the state persists after a restart.

features.name: Distinguishing no data / incomplete / Skip
steps: Enable "show question marks for missing data"
No data, explicit failure, success, and Skip use different states
Backfilling a past date converts it from "unknown" to an explicit record
The statistics are recomputed accordingly
features.expected: The four states—no data, failure, success, and Skip—must be distinguishable in the UI; "unknown" data must not be counted as failure; after backfilling history the state converts and the statistics are recomputed; the toggle only changes the display without modifying existing records.

features.name: The logical date across midnight
steps: Enable "extend the day by a few hours after midnight"
Records made after midnight are still assigned to the previous day
The new day only begins after the app-configured day boundary
The date columns, reminders, and history use a unified logical date
features.expected: When enabled, records made after midnight must be assigned to the previous day and only enter the new day past the configured day boundary; the date columns, reminders, and statistics must use the same logical date, and the same record must not appear on two dates at once.

features.name: Archiving and restoring habits
steps: Archive a Habit that is no longer tracked
The default list can hide it, but the historical data still exists
It reappears after disabling "hide archived"
Unarchive restores it as an active Habit rather than creating a copy. The official FAQ/discussions confirm that archived Habits can be restored again. GitHub
features.expected: Archiving only changes the display state and the historical data must be preserved; unarchiving must restore the same Habit rather than creating a copy; the "hide archived" toggle immediately affects the list; it persists after a restart.

features.name: Completed-state filtering
steps: Enable "hide completed"
A Habit already completed in the current period is hidden from the main list
Incomplete items remain visible
After changing the day's state the Habit can dynamically enter/leave the filtered results
The data itself is not deleted by hiding
features.expected: The filtering must be determined dynamically by the current period's completion state; after a state change the Habit immediately enters or leaves the list; filtering only affects the display and must not delete or modify any habit data.

features.name: Multi-rule sorting and manual order
steps: Create several Habits with different names, colors, scores, and states
Switch between "manual / by name / by color / by score / by state"
The order is recomputed for each mode
When switching back to manual the user-maintained custom order is restored
features.expected: Each sort must genuinely reorder the list by the corresponding field; switching back to manual must restore the user-maintained custom order; the manual order and sort-mode settings persist; sorting does not change any habit data.

features.name: Habit Score derived computation
steps: Complete the Habit on consecutive days
The Score gradually increases
It gradually decreases after several consecutive misses
After modifying a past day's record the current Score is recomputed

The Score is not a directly saved static percentage. The official documentation states that the Score is computed with exponential smoothing over the whole history, weighting recent records more heavily. GitHub
features.expected: The Score must be derived from the whole history with recent records weighted more heavily and must not be a manually saved static value; after modifying past records the current Score must be recomputed; consecutive completions raise it and misses lower it.

features.name: Habit details and multi-timescale statistics
steps: Tap the Habit name
Open the details
View the overview, score chart, history, and calendar
Switch between day/week/month granularities
After adding a record the success rate, monthly/yearly changes, totals, and charts change in sync
features.expected: The values in the details page's overview, score chart, history, and calendar must come from the same set of records and be mutually consistent; after adding or modifying records all statistics and charts update in sync; the day, week, and month views use the same data source.

features.name: Periodic-goal statistics for a quantifiable Habit
steps: For example, a daily goal of 10
The details page shows derived goals such as "today 10 / week 70 / month ~300 / quarter ~910 / year ~3.7k" according to the frequency
After changing the base goal or frequency all periodic goals are recomputed
features.expected: Periodic goals must be derived from the daily goal and frequency, e.g. 10 per day corresponds to about 70/week and 300/month; after changing the base goal or frequency all periodic values are recomputed in sync and keep consistent proportions.

features.name: History backfill and correction
steps: Enter history/calendar from the Habit details
Modify the completion, failure, Skip, or value of a past day
Save
The day's history changes
The current Score, charts, totals, streak, and other statistics are recomputed. The official FAQ explicitly allows backfilling past dates in the detail calendar. GitHub
features.expected: Backfilling must write into the real history; after modifying a day, derived statistics such as the Score, streak, charts, and totals are all recomputed; records on different dates do not contaminate one another and persist after a restart.

features.name: Per-Habit reminders and notification behavior
steps: Set a reminder time for the Habit
A notification is produced at the time if not yet completed
Completion/ignore actions are available from the notification
If it was already completed before the reminder, that reminder does not appear
Different Habits have independent reminders. The official documentation clearly states that each Habit can have its own reminder and can be acted on directly from the notification. GitHub
features.expected: A reminder must only trigger when the day is not yet completed; after completion no repeated notification at the time; a completion from the notification must match the in-app state; different Habits' reminder times are independent.

features.name: Global notification configuration
steps: Configure notification persistence, default/silent, sound, vibration, notification dots, "Do Not Disturb" override, etc.
Subsequent Habit reminders are presented according to the global rules
Disabling notifications stops the visual reminders while the Habit data and schedule themselves are preserved
features.expected: The global notification settings must genuinely affect how reminders are presented; after disabling notifications no reminders are produced, but the Habit schedule, records, and statistics are unaffected; the settings persist across restarts.

features.name: Full backup, restore, and data migration
steps: Create several Habits and accumulate history
"Export full backup" produces a data file that can be imported again
Import a backup after modifying/deleting data

Habit definitions, history, and statistics are restored to the backup state; CSV export is for spreadsheet analysis, while Import Data also supports the app's own backups and the migration sources listed in the screenshot such as Tickmate / HabitBull / Rewire. The official documentation clearly distinguishes Full Backup from CSV Export
features.expected: The exported full backup must be re-importable and restore the Habit definitions, history, and statistics; the import must validate the file format, and an abnormal file must not damage existing data; CSV export is only for analysis and cannot serve as a restore source.
